chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who could not find a sacrificial animal. He said: 'He should fast three days during Hajj: one day before the Day of Tarwiyah, the Day of Tarwiyah, and the Day of Arafah.' I said: 'If that day passes for him?' He said: 'He should eat suhoor on the night of al-Hasbah and fast that day and two days after it.' I said: 'If his camel does not stay with him (i.e., he is traveling without his mount), should he fast them on the road?' He said: 'If he wishes, he fasts them on the road, and if he wishes, (he delays) until he returns to his people.'
If he does not fast these three days in Dhu al-Hijjah until the new moon of Muharram appears, then upon him is the blood of a sheep (damm), and there is no fasting for him. He narrated that.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina.
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: The blood/expiation of a sheep, a specific form of fidya.
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the day of standing at Arafat.
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْحَصْبَةِ: The night of the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah, after stoning the Jamarat.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, keeping the ihram between them.
key_terms.هَدْيًا: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim.

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who cannot afford a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the graduated fidya for Hajj al-Tamattu', prioritizing fasting three days during Dhu al-Hijjah as a substitute for the sacrificial animal (had'y). It highlights the jurisprudential flexibility granted to travelers, allowing them to delay the fast until their return if necessary, while establishing a strict deadline: if the three days are not completed before Muharram begins, the obligation shifts irrevocably to offering a sheep. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease in worship while maintaining the structural integrity of Hajj rituals.
